Subject: Inquiry: baseline spend and pilot activation credits for hosted API

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput looked promising for the summarization pipelines we'll run. Procurement asked me to get clarity on two practical items before we move this to budget: 1) do you have a minimum monthly spend or floor for hosted API customers doing pilots (we don't plan to buy Dedicated right now), and 2) do you offer any activation/pilot credits or short-term rate protections while we validate quality?

Our pilot is scoped to ~50M tokens over 30 days across staging+prod calls. We also need a simple SOW template and an initial rate card to show to our finance team. I've attached a short doc with expected call patterns.

Can you share options (no need to be final numbers) and any standard contractual caveats for pilots?

Thanks,

Hi Sara — really appreciated the time yesterday. Quick answers up front, then a few options: 

Short answer: we do not require a Dedicated commitment for pilots. For hosted API pilots we typically offer one of three structures depending on customer preference: 

- Activation credit model: a one-time pilot credit (e.g., $15k) applied against usage for the first 30–45 days. No monthly minimum during the credit period; unit rates are our public hosted rates.

- Baseline reservation (soft): a 3-month rolling baseline reserved at a modest discount (5–12%) with the first month billed pro-rata. This provides rate protection for you if usage spikes but has a small minimum (e.g., $5k/month). Credits towards committed baseline are possible if you convert to a longer-term reserved plan.

- Usage cushion + volume ladder: no formal minimum, but we offer step discounts once you cross token thresholds within a billing period (e.g., 50M, 200M). We can frontload a small activation credit and guarantee the first threshold pricing for the pilot period.

Attachments I can share: a short pilot SOW template and a preliminary rate card. Monica, can you attach the SOW draft and the tiered pricing sheet for Sara? Aditya — can you confirm the 50M token example and any recommended rate guarantee for that band?

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inquiry: baseline spend and pilot activation credits for hosted API

Hi Sara — attaching the pilot SOW draft and a concise rate sheet. Summary notes: 

- Pilot activation credit: typical range we offer is $10k–$20k depending on PO timing and evaluation scope. Credits reduce your first invoice; if you convert to a 12-month reserved contract within 60 days we apply an additional conversion credit.

- Baseline reserve: for teams that need predictable monthly cost we offer a 3-month soft reserve starting at $5k/month (5% discount) or $15k/month (12% discount). These are refundable as credits if you scale into Dedicated.

- Non-production allowances: we can mark a portion of usage as evaluation (staging) and apply a lower unit rate for a capped amount to ease validation costs — usually up to 10% of pilot tokens.

I've put rough example math in the attached SOW so finance can see line items. Happy to hop on a call with procurement and your engineering lead to walk through.

Attachment: SOW_draft_BW_20261101.docx (docx)

Best,
Monica

Thanks, Monica — the SOW looks sensible. A few follow-ups from procurement/finance: 

1) Can the activation credit be applied as an invoice credit rather than up-front payment? Procurement prefers credits applied to invoices rather than vendor rebates.
2) For the baseline reserve option, will you accept a quarterly PO (instead of monthly invoices) for the reserved amount?
3) If we convert to a 12-month reserved contract, can you commit to a fixed unit rate for 90 days post-conversion to ease forecasting?

Also our engineering manager asked whether the non-production allowance can be scoped to calls tagged with a header (we can tag staging traffic). That would help us measure staging vs prod precisely.

If you can confirm these items we'll get procurement to draft an LOI.

—Sara
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Sara Li <sara.li@bluewavehealth.com>, procurement@bluewavehealth.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: baseline spend and pilot activation credits for hosted API

Sara — short answers below, happy to bake into the SOW language: 

1) Activation credit handling: yes — we can issue an invoice credit that reduces your bill rather than requiring prepayment. We'll include standard expiration language (60 days) in the SOW.

2) Quarterly PO: acceptable. We can take a quarterly PO for the reserved baseline and bill monthly internally; the PO just needs to reference the SOW and line items. Finance will provide a simple PO template if needed.

3) Post-conversion rate lock: we can guarantee the unit rate for 90 days post-conversion for customers who move to a 12-month reserved plan within the pilot window. That will be explicitly stated in the conversion addendum.

4) Tagging staging traffic: yes — we support an HTTP header (X-Environment: staging) that we can use to categorize usage for non-production allowances. Our billing team will accept a short mapping table.

Next steps: Monica to finalize the SOW and include the activation credit as an invoice credit line, Aditya to confirm the pilot rate guarantee for the 50M band, and Sara if you can share a PO template timeline we will mirror that in the SOW. If helpful, we can do a 30-minute procurement alignment call tomorrow.

Thanks — excited to get this pilot running.

Markus Klein
